newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm after U.S. CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm after U.S. CPI data.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds firmed on Tuesday on a smaller-than-expected rise in the U.S. March consumer price index, which eased market fears of a U.S. interest rate hike, dealers said.
They said the market ignored earlier news about Russia's plans to issue another Eurobond in the near future.
MinFins closely track Brady Bonds and other emerging market debt. Fears of a possible U.S. interest rate rise in May have pressured emerging market prices.
The U.S. Labor Department said the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.1 percent in March, below forecasts of 0.2 percent and below a 0.3 percent increase in February.

First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Tuesday Russia planned to return to international capital markets soon with a dollar Eurobond. The bond, running for at least five years, would be issued through SBC Warburg and JP Morgan.

"The market saw CPI data as positive and prices firmed 0.15-0.20 points at average," an ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said. "But it does not imply an upward trend has begun, it seems just a correction."
Dealers said no impact had been seen earlier on the market on Russia's Eurobond plans as the MinFins, like other emerging markets, are bound to track U.S. Treasuries moves.

"The day was quiet until (U.S.) CPI figures," one dealer said. "There was no reaction on Eurobonds, as what is more important for the market is what they are going to do with interest rates in the U.S."
